newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares snap losing streak, end firm.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares snap losing streak, end firm.

text.p: Chilean blue chips snapped a four-day losing streak run to close stronger in line with the rally on Wall Street, traders said.
Dealers said the positive mood should boost stocks at the opening with turnover similar to Thursday.
The 40-share index ended up 0.53 percent at 133.09 points. The general index firmed 0.43 percent to 5,756.19 points.
Volume swelled to 13 billion pesos from 11.4 billion pesos Thursday.
Traders noted Chilean ADRs firmed on the back of the 0.76 percent rally in the Dow Jones Industrial Index after a three-session losing streak in New York.
"The recovery in New York translated into a slight increase in demand for Chilean ADRs in the morning," said one broker.
Leading gainers included companies linked to businessman Manuel Cruzat, CB Inversiones and CB Capitales, which rose sharply in a correction to falls last week.
CB Inversiones climbed 15.9 percent to 12.75 pesos while CB Capitales rose 10.4 percent to 13.8 pesos.
Losers included telecom Telex, down 3.57 percent at 1,080 pesos and fertilizer-maker Soquimich which shed 1.76 percent to 2,505 pesos.
